$comment: Academy family (docs/map-briefs/st_johns, step 1): a dormitory floor in bays, for halls of any length on one, two or three floors. A hall is a row of Dorm Bays (1 × 2 cells: the hall down the middle, two rooms each side) between two Stair End Bays, with the Dorm Office Bay in the middle. All run west to east in their own frame, the hall's middle on the line between the two rows of cells (4 m north of the anchor cell's centre), 2.4 m wide at every bay's ends. Parts as in carriageway.json; parts are only ever added at the end. Edit, then run `node tools/content/setpieces.mjs`.

notes.design: Two Rooms open to each other and at both ends; the hall straddles the line between them (z 2.8 to 5.2 m from the anchor cell's centre). Its walls are blocks 0.72 m thick, a closet deep: three piers a side to the doors' heads (2.6 m) and one beam over them, so each room's 2 m doorway is a reveal 0.6 m deep between two built-in closets (2 m: bots keep 0.8 m off walls). The closets are the wall: a Built-in Closet Front (a still prop, 12 mm proud, no collision) in its face either side of the doorway. A partition 0.12 m thick between the two rooms of a side, and half a partition at each end, so two bays side by side make a whole one. Rooms are 3.88 m wide and 6.18 m from the hall wall to the window (5.58 m past the closets). Each: an Oak Door standing open in the reveal (a still prop, no collision), a sink unit on the left 0.9 m past the closet's front (the closet door has room), two desks with hutches along the left wall (the second by the window), a chair pushed in at each (not solid), a bunk on the right by the window (Twin sash windows, one a room). Clear floor: 2.08 m between the desks and the bunk, 1.93 m between a chair's back and the bunk. One light, in the hall. A room's pieces are in one order for the four rooms, so a placement can hide a room's furniture by part index.

notes.design: Scott Johnston / Hazelwood's centre (docs/map-briefs/st_johns, PLAN_2026-11-12.md 3.2, step 3): two cells of hall on three floors with the block in front of them. North of the hall on each floor the Dorm Bay's two rooms a cell (doors wide or slim, the Room doors option); south of it an open landing the width of both cells, through a 6 m opening between short piers on each cell (as the Dorm Entry Bay's). The forward block (the cells a cell south): a half-turn Stairwell west from the ground to the first floor, the entrance hall east under a Round arch (benches, plants), a second Stairwell over the entrance hall from the first floor to the second (a Stairwell takes two levels of its cell, so they alternate cells, as in the Stair End Bay (3 floors)), and a room over the first with twin sashes south. Every stair opens north onto the landings. The forward block wears the hall's facade on its three outer sides, its top floor a twin sash and an arched window. Ends: half partitions at the landings' ends, so the Dorm Bays beside it close them; the hall's mouths meet theirs on every floor. Turrets: a Round Corner Turret in the cell either side of the forward block.

notes.design: A solid round turret of blocks in the cell's south-east corner (its centre 1.75 m in from the cell's east and south edges, so its cone's eaves stay in the cell: it stands 0.25 m off a hall on the cell's east side, over the facade's corner buttress, and 0.25 m behind that hall's south front): twelve wall faces of the look's stone 0.5 m thick, a dressed cornice at 14 m and a cap over the hollow inside: 25 blocks and its top, kept few because a map as played holds at most 4,096 entities (St. John's is near it). Top (an option): merlons on every other face of the cornice, or the Conical Turret Roof (kit.roof.cone) in slate or red shingle. Nobody gets in: it is a landmark and cover.

notes.design: St. John's step 6 (PLAN 3.2 D, Welles's mess hall): the room is the two cells of the bay with no wall between them (16 m across, 8 m along), so bays end to end make one long hall; the hall's ends are what it meets (a Stair End Bay's mouth). The long walls are a choice (option Long walls): arched windows (the default), a round-arched way in on one side or both, or a solid wall with the fireplace (a cold hearth of blocks: nothing burns, glows or flickers). The piers stand at the bay's west end, so a row of bays has one every 8 m. Step 7a: Main entrance north / south (the Twin arches wall style, format v49) is the hall's door from outside, two arches on a middle pier; the south banner hangs only where the south wall is not that entrance (a `when` list). The plan's floor sunk half a metre is not built (MapMaker's sunken centre is refused on the ground: no room under it); the hall is the level's 3.5 m.
notes.step7d: St. John's step 7d (the owner's sketch and photos 6 and 7, OWNER_NOTES_2026-11-21). Every new option's first choice is the bay as it was, so placements made before keep their look. Floor Sunk 0.5 m: the tiles are Sunk Rooms (core.room_sunk: the slab half a metre down, the ground cut out of the cell), a footing 0.6 m wide under each long wall whose top is the doorways' threshold, one step of 0.25 m, half a metre deep, inside every doorway (4 m wide at a round arch, 7 m at the twin arches), the wall piers and the long walls' fireplaces on feet; furniture stands half a metre lower (each floor-standing part is listed for both floors). Ceiling Timber beams: kit.roof.timber_bay under the ceiling (beams over the bay's ends and its middle: over the arcade's piers). Side aisle Arcade south: kit.wall.arcade along z = 0 (half a pier at each end of the bay and a whole one in its middle, arches 3 m: a round-arched south door faces the middle pier, the twin arches face the two arches), its foot 0.45 m under the floor so one model serves both floors; the aisle is 3.1 m deep, the main hall 11.1 m. Furniture Rows (and Rows with a podium: a kit.table.lectern and a kit.monument.bell_stand against the north wall): kit.table.mess, four rows at z 1.85, 4.66, 7.47 and 10.28, evenly spaced as the photographs show them, with three aisles of 2.05 m between them (what bots need; the middle one is on the fireplace), 1.07 m between the first row and the arcade and the last row's chairs by the north wall's piers: bots keep to those aisles and reach the side aisle only through a bay whose aisle has no small tables (one with a way in on its south side, by its cross aisle), players walk in anywhere; two tables a row; the west table of each row is left out unless the West end is Open. Rows with a cross aisle: kit.table.mess_small at each end of the bay. The aisle's small tables stand only where the south wall has no way in. West end: Steps up is one step across the end between the footings; the end walls are blocks (0.45 m, a hair under the ceiling); the fireplace wall is kit.wall.fireplace between two kit.wall.panel_window, centred on the main hall (z 5.95 with the arcade, 4 without), scaled 0.96 on a level floor to stand under a 3.5 m ceiling, with one steady light at the hearth. Parts under the level's floor: map/setPieceCheck.ts allows a part up to 1 m under the piece's lowest floor.

notes.design: St. John's step 7d (the owner's sketch: the kitchen at the far left, the full depth of the room, behind the line). A Refectory Bay's shell (arched windows both sides, so a hall's outside keeps its rhythm) between two cross walls of blocks: the west one 0.3 m thick with a doorway 2.4 m wide and 2.4 m high at the bay's middle (z 2.8 to 5.2) onto the serving line's staff side; the east one 0.45 m thick, solid, or with the same doorway (East end, Back door: where a Stair End Bay's mouth is; a step in the doorway over a sunk floor). Cross walls are blocks so the piece works in the middle of a hall's cells (a side's wall style would stand on the floor's own level and leave a gap under it over a sunk floor). Equipment, all models the kit had: three Stoves and two Fridges along the east wall, three Kitchen Cabinets as a prep counter, two Shelf Ends (boxes) on the south wall either side of the window; new: the walk-in cooler's door (kit.door.walk_in, a still prop on the east wall). One ceiling light.

notes.design: St. John's step 6 (PLAN 3.2 D; Q4: beside the bridge at Welles's west end). The tower is the Clock Tower tile (map/packTiles2.ts, gothic.clock_tower: walls, stair, belfry and parapet are tile boxes, so the tower costs no entities); the piece dresses it in its pack's stone and trim and hangs a Clock Face (kit.sign.clock_face) on each side of the stage under the belfry, their feet 14 m up. One light lights the stair. The faces' hands are fixed: nothing moves, glows or blinks (Reduce flashing).

pieces.displayName: Stair End Bay (3 floors, roof stair)
pieces.blurb: A three-floor Stair End Bay whose stair goes on up to the roof: a third half-turn stairwell over the first, under a stair head, out onto the roof over the lobby's side; the hall's mouth east on every floor.

choices.label: At the hall's end
choices.blurb: A 1.5 m oak door in the first floor's outer wall beside the hall's mouth, over the lobby's door: where a bridge's upper door meets a three-floor hall (bots go through on a link).

notes.design: St. John's step 7b (DeKoven's roof perch: PLAN_2026-11-12.md 3.3, a way up to the roof of a three-floor hall). The Stair End Bay (3 floors) with a third Stairwell where its top landing room was, over the first and turned the same way: its foot opens north on the top floor (where the second stair lands), its upper landing opens north at roof height onto the roof over the second stairwell, which is the piece's own roof block (its top at 12 m, level with the roofs of a hall's top-floor rooms: walk on east along the hall). The stair head is the Stairwell's upper storey: walls on its three other sides (a sash window south), a plaster ceiling and a roof block over it at 15.5 m, a floor block closing the landing's open corner and a rail over the flight, as on the floors below. It claims four levels (the head stands a storey above the roof). First-floor door as the three-floor bay's.

pieces.blurb: A hall's bay with the stair down to its basement, 1 × 2 cells: the hall runs through on the ground floor past a half-turn stairwell; below, a lobby with the basement hall's mouth east. Place it at the ground floor.

choices.label: Left for the floor above

notes.design: St. John's step 7b (DeKoven's basement of offices: PLAN_2026-11-12.md 3.3, a stair down inside). The Stair End Bay's stairwell (as the Basement Stairwell tile, which cuts the ground out of its own cell) and lobby a level down, and the bay a way through on the ground floor: the Stairwell (turned so its foot and upper landing open north) climbs from the basement lobby to the ground floor, where its landing strip (z 1.9 to 4 m) and the room north of it carry the hall (z 2.8 to 5.2 m) from the west mouth to the east one; walls of its own close both ends but for the mouths, and the east end of the basement but for the basement hall's mouth. The landing's open corner is closed by a floor block out to the west wall, a rail stands over the flight. Basement walls are solid and wear no facade (they are in the ground; the lobby is a Basement Room, which like the stairwell cuts the ground out of its own cell). Over the stair (an option): a ceiling and roof of its own, or nothing, for a bay placed on the floor above. Place it at the ground floor's level; it claims the level below.
